claims.body: It’s the Wild’s second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Canucks get more of the play than usual.

claims.head: Who drives the play: the Wild
claims.body: The Wild have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Canucks the worst. Expect the Wild to spend more of the night in the Canucks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Marcus Foligno is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.
Brock Faber is on injured reserve (skull surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-pair defenseman. Jared Spurgeon has taken his spot beside Quinn Hughes.
Tyler Pitlick was added to the roster on Oct 13 and has played beside Michael McCarron and Rieger Lorenz.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 44%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Max Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 35% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, up from 4% last season.

stakes: The Wild go in tied for first in the Central with 16 points, the Canucks eighth in the Pacific with 5 points.

VAN.head: The Canucks have their work cut out
VAN.body: Even though Minnesota is on the second night of a back-to-back and Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Canucks’ best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night from Leevi Meriläinen.

MIN.head: The Wild should be in control
MIN.body: Even though Minnesota is on the second night of a back-to-back and Vancouver has home-ice advantage, the Wild have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. If the Canucks want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

story.head: Something has to change for the Canucks
paras: The Canucks are winless in nine (0-8-1). The Wild are 7-3-2.
The Wild usually control more of the chances than the Canucks do. The Wild shoot a lot, and the Canucks give up plenty.

items.text: Quinn Hughes is one point from 500.
The Wild have been without Marcus Foligno since Oct 8, and have had to make do without Filip Gustavsson and Brock Faber all season. Calvin Pickard is expected to start.
The Canucks have been without Thatcher Demko all season. Leevi Meriläinen is expected to start.
Kirill Kaprizov has five goals in eight games against Vancouver since 2023-24.
